subject: Observability acceptance criteria & escalation lane alignment — GridScale deployment
messages:
From: Aaron Park <aaron.park@gridscale.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>; support@redwood.com
Cc: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@gridscale.io>
Date: 2027-08-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observability acceptance criteria for go-live

Sean / Redwood team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re pacing our production cutover to your hosted API for September 1st and need to lock acceptance criteria for observability before then. Specifically GridScale needs: dashboards showing model latency percentiles by route, tracing hooks that include request_id + model_version, a clear error taxonomy (user error vs model failure vs infra), and an alerting matrix that maps severity to oncall lanes and escalation steps.

Can you share a proposed acceptance matrix and owner assignments for dashboards/runbooks? Ideally we can iterate over the next two weeks and freeze before the final rollout dry run.

Attachments: none yet

Thanks,
Aaron Park
Platform Engineering Lead, GridScale
aaron.park@gridscale.io

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Park <aaron.park@gridscale.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability acceptance criteria for go-live

Aaron —

Great; thanks for the clear list. I attached an initial acceptance matrix that maps each requirement to a pass/fail condition, suggested SLOs, and an owner from our side. High level plan:

- This week: align on acceptance criteria and owner roster
- Next week: telemetry wiring and dashboard templates deployed to your staging project
- Aug 30: dry run with synthetic traffic and runbook walkthrough
- Sept 1: go-live if dry run passes

Quick notes on your asks:
- Dashboards: we’ll deliver a dashboard bundle (latency p50/p95/p99 by route, error rate, token throughput). Owner: laura.bennett (dashboard + alert queries).
- Tracing hooks: snippet included (tracing-hook-snippet.patch) that instruments request_id and model_version; owner: monica.patel (tracing hooks + KV cache propagation).
- Error taxonomy: included in the matrix; we separate user_input_errors, model_generation_errors, infra_timeouts, and config_mismatch; owner: ben.carter (runbook taxonomy + escalation steps).
- Alert routing: propose three severity lanes (P1: oncall + escalate to SRE manager; P2: emailed rotation; P3: ticketing only).

Attached: observability-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (sheet with criteria), tracing-hook-snippet.patch (example code), runbook-escalation-lanes.md (draft lanes).

Can Laura / Monica / Ben chime in with any adjustments to owners or timing?

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Customer Success / Technical Onboarding
Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: observability-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
--- Attachment: tracing-hook-snippet.patch (text patch)
--- Attachment: runbook-escalation-lanes.md (markdown)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Aaron Park <aaron.park@gridscale.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-17T12:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability acceptance criteria for go-live

Thanks Sean — quick alignment notes from my side on dashboards/alerts: 

1) Dashboard scope: I’ll create a dedicated GridScale folder in our dashboard repo and push four panels: route latency heatmap, model_version breakdown, token throughput, and error taxonomy rollup.
2) Alert queries: prefer rate-based alerts on a sliding 5m window for P1/P2; static thresholds for P3 (informational). I’ll send proposed query examples by EOD Thursday.
3) Ownership & RCA: propose that GridScale SRE owns triage for config_mismatch and user_input_errors; Redwood SRE owns model_generation_errors and infra_timeouts (we can route the first notification to their SRE rotation and require a joint triage within 30 minutes for P1s).

Small ask: can GridScale provide a sample request_id pattern and a short list of model_versions you expect to run in staging? That helps us parameterize dashboards and tracing tags.

Laura Bennett
Observability Lead, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

> On 2027-08-17 11:03, Sean Gallagher wrote:
> > Attached: observability-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (sheet with criteria), tracing-hook-snippet.patch (example code), runbook-escalation-lanes.md (draft lanes).

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aaron Park <aaron.park@gridscale.io>
Date: 2027-08-18T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability acceptance criteria for go-live

Looping in specifics on runbooks and taxonomy. I updated the attached runbook-escalation-lanes.md with concrete playbooks for each error class:

- user_input_errors: quick rejection with context + customer-facing note; severity P3 unless amplified
- model_generation_errors: immediate P1 if model halts or returns invalid JSON; fallback to smaller model variant where configured
- infra_timeouts: P1 with automatic circuit-breaker on per-route basis
- config_mismatch: P2 with automated detection and rollback playbook

I also added an "Acceptance checklist" section to the matrix that requires: dashboards populated, tracing hooks visible in staging traces, first failure RCA run in staging, and alert routing tested with PagerDuty simulation.

Notes on simulation: Monica — can you schedule a 1-hour slot next Tuesday (Aug 24) to run the synthetic traffic and simulate a P1 model_generation_error so we can validate the runbook and oncall workflow?

Ben Carter
Technical Solutions, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

--- Attachment: runbook-escalation-lanes.md (updated draft)

From: Aaron Park <aaron.park@gridscale.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@gridscale.io>
Date: 2027-08-19T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability acceptance criteria for go-live

Sean / team —

This looks good and aligned with our needs. Quick confirmations:

- GridScale will provide a list of 4 model_versions and the request_id regex by EOD tomorrow.
- We accept the owner split (GridScale SRE: config/user errors; Redwood SRE: model/infra).
- We’ll block Aug 24 10:00–11:00 PT for the synthetic P1 simulation and invite our oncall.

If the dry run passes your acceptance checklist (dashboards, tracing, simulation), GridScale will proceed with September 1 cutover. Appreciate the clarity — can you send a short calendar invite with the runbook doc attached?

Thanks,
Aaron
